title: Pollution Driven by U.S. Data Centers Causing Hundreds of Early Deaths
summary: U.S. data centers are driving greater power demand, and with it, more pollution from coal and gas power plants. Researchers estimate that worsening pollution is leading to hundreds of early deaths.Read more on E360 →

The new modeling study finds that, in 2023, the added power demand from data centers led to an estimated 650 early deaths across the U.S. Given the rapid buildout of data centers, their impact would likely be even greater today, authors say.

The study further suggests that pollution is often intensifying far from where data centers are located. For instance, data centers in Virginia — which are connected to a large regional power grid — might spur power plants in the Midwest to ramp up. As their power output grows, so does particulate pollution, a contaminant linked to heart attacks, strokes, and lung disease.
